summary: No security findings. The only new input is the native <select id="config-stake">. Its onChange handler checks event.target.value against an allowlist: CASH_STAKES.find(s => stakeKey(s) === value). An unknown or tampered DOM value (for example an <option> edited in devtools to '0/-5', '1e9/2e9', or a non-string) matches nothing and is ignored (`if (chosen !== undefined)`). So the only values that can reach setStake, and through it onStart({...config, stake}), are the six deeply frozen CASH_STAKES objects. A tampered option can never produce a stake that is negative, zero, NaN, non-numeric or shaped differently. The initial stake comes from the trusted caller (config.stake), not from the DOM. The option text is rendered as React text children, so nothing reaches an HTML sink. The CSS data: URI is a static, hard-coded SVG chevron with no interpolated values. An SVG used as a CSS background image cannot run script, so it adds no injection surface. There are no new dependencies, network calls, storage, secrets or randomness. There are no money or real-payment flows: values are play-money labels only, and SPEC-06/SPEC-09 assert there is no deposit, payment or cash-out text or control. The change fails closed.
